Crans's 2014 McMaster MSc thesis (MacSphere, open), whose Chapter 3 presents the same sunfish hypoxia-temperature experiments as 'preliminary data' (Crans is the article's second author)

Comparative Biochemistry and Physiology Part A 198: 59–71 (1 August 2016), doi:10.1016/j.cbpa.2016.04.010. The entry agrees.

claims.claim: pumpkinseed take ≥ 2× bluegill's time to lose equilibrium at 2 kPa O₂
claims.note: Full text not read. The abstract (not usable to confirm) agrees but with a condition the table omits: time to LOE was measured in sustained hypoxia at PO2 2 kPa, and pumpkinseed had ≥ 2-fold longer time to LOE than bluegill and hybrids 'across this temperature range' (15–25 °C), while their greater tolerance 'collapsed at 28°C'. Add '(15–25 °C; not at 28 °C)'. STAND-IN: Crans 2014 MSc thesis (see notes) Fig. 3-1D shows the same pattern at a constant 1.0 mg O2/L: pumpkinseed ≈ 580 vs bluegill ≈ 250 min at 15 °C, ≈ 69 vs ≈ 31 min at 25 °C, ≈ 43 vs ≈ 29 min at 28 °C (my reading of the figure; ratios ≈ 2.3, 2.2, 1.5); its text: 'Pumpkinseed sunfish have a longer time to LOE across all experimental temperatures' (p. 49, PDF p. 59).

notes: Stand-in, read in full: Crans, K. D. 2014. Mechanisms, evolution, and phenotypic plasticity of hypoxia tolerance among bass and sunfish (family Centrarchidae). MSc thesis, McMaster University (MacSphere handle 11375/16349; PDF https://prod-ms-be.lib.mcmaster.ca/server/api/core/bitstreams/ce9a90c8-6934-45bf-9092-b398377b1ad3/content; saved as Borowiec_etal_2016.standin-Crans2014MSc.pdf). Chapter 3 ('The effects of temperature on hypoxia tolerance', p. 45, PDF p. 55): lab-acclimated (12–15 °C) pumpkinseed, bluegill and hybrids tested at 15, 25 and 28 °C; time to LOE at a constant 1.0 mg O2/L; pumpkinseed most tolerant by time to LOE but most sensitive to warming, with a higher Pcrit than bluegill at 28 °C. It supports the direction and the ≈ 2× ratio at 15–25 °C, but at 1.0 mg O2/L, not 2 kPa, and as preliminary data. Cite the 2016 article for the 2-kPa figure once read, or cite the thesis with its own test condition. Chapter 2 compares exercise and hypoxia tolerance across largemouth bass, rock bass, pumpkinseed and bluegill.
